mainTopic: Vouching for new-moon witnesses, the בייתוסין plot, and the torch signals for ראש חודש (ראש השנה כב:)
overview: The amud opens by asking how many people must vouch for a witness to the new moon whom בית דין does not know. רב פפא explains that the משנה's 'another' means another pair, and the משנה's word 'אותו' proves this. The story of רבי נהוראי seems to show one voucher is enough, but the גמרא answers that a second voucher was there, and learns that שבת may be broken for עדות החודש even in a case of doubt. עולא and רב כהנא teach that one ordinary person is believed to report that בית דין already declared the month, because people do not lie about things that will come out. A ברייתא then tells how the בייתוסין bribed false witnesses, which led to the rule that only witnesses known to בית דין are accepted. A new משנה describes the old system of signal torches passed from mountain to mountain until the whole גולה was lit, and how the כותים' fake torches forced a switch to messengers. The גמרא proves that משיאין means kindling, and a ברייתא teaches that torches were lit only after a short month. רבי זירא begins to explain this as a גזירה because of ראש חודש on ערב שבת, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can a single person be trusted to vouch for a witness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's word 'another': one person should not be enough, and a ברייתא speaks of 'his witnesses' in the plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is one person believed? Doesn't a ברייתא say: There was a case where the witness came, and his witnesses came with him to vouch for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the משנה, which said to send 'another' (one person) with an unknown witness. It brings a ברייתא that uses the plural 'his witnesses', which suggests two are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vouching for a witness is a form of testimony, and testimony normally needs two עדים. The ברייתא's plural wording 'וְעֵדָיו' shows that two people came to vouch. So the משנה's singular 'אחר' looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge from a source)
to testify about him, to vouch for him

steps.confusionAlert: The 'witness' here is the person who saw the new moon. 'His witnesses' are the people vouching that he is a trustworthy person. They are not testifying about the moon itself.

phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה's 'משלחין אחר עמו' (they send another with him).

phrases.english: But it was taught: There was an incident where he came
he and his witnesses with him

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's wording 'אחר' from the previous section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's singular 'אחר' (another one) sent to vouch for the witness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Testimony requires two, and a ברייתא uses the plural 'his witnesses', so one should not suffice.

steps.title: רב פפא: 'Another' means another pair
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reinterprets the משנה's 'another' as 'another pair' of witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: What does 'another' mean? Another pair.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by rereading the משנה. The word 'another' really means another pair of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not saying one person is enough. 'אחר' refers to another unit of testimony, which is a pair. Now the משנה and the ברייתא agree that two vouchers are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא, a sage of the גמרא

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אחר' means another pair of witnesses, so two are required.

steps.title: Support from the word 'him' in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to prove רב פפא's reading from another word in the same משנה: 'אותו' (him).
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. For if you don't say so, the משנה says 'if they do not recognize him' — what does 'him' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof for רב פפא. It points to the word 'אותו' in the משנה and asks what it refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by showing that a singular word in this משנה ('אותו') must already mean a pair. If that is true, the singular 'אחר' can also mean a pair.

keyTerms.meaning: this also stands to reason (introduces logical support)
for if you do not say so

phrases.english: for if you do not say so —

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins supporting רב פפא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's reading that 'אחר' means a pair.

steps.title: 'Him' cannot mean a single witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects reading 'אותו' as one witness, because the new moon is called 'משפט' and judgment requires two.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say 'him' means one witness — is one witness believed? The word 'judgment' is written about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible meaning of 'אותו', a single witness, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls קידוש החודש a 'משפט' (judgment), and every judgment needs two עדים. So a single person who saw the moon could never be accepted. 'Him' therefore cannot mean one witness.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (proposes an option to reject)

phrases.notes: תהלים פא:ה, 'כי חק לישראל הוא משפט לאלקי יעקב'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Eliminates one option for the question in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading of 'אותו' as a single witness.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A judgment (משפט) requires two witnesses, so one could never testify.

steps.title: 'Him' means that pair, so 'another' means another pair
steps.stepSummary: Since 'אותו' must mean 'that pair', 'אחר' in the same משנה means 'another pair'. רב פפא is supported.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is 'him'? That pair. So too, what is 'another'? Another pair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes the proof. Singular words in this משנה refer to pairs, so 'another' means another pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses singular language to speak about a set of witnesses. Since 'אותו' must mean the pair who saw the moon, reading 'אחר' as another pair fits the same style. This confirms רב פפא.
steps.whatToRemember: Both the witnesses to the moon and the people vouching for them must be pairs. The משנה's singular words ('אותו', 'אחר') each refer to a pair.

phrases.notes: The גמרא itself repeats רב פפא's words, here as the conclusion of the proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'אחר' in the משנה means another pair, as רב פפא said.

steps.title: The story of רבי נהוראי seems to show one is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the two-person rule from a ברייתא where רבי נהוראי alone went to vouch for a witness in אושא on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is one not believed? But a ברייתא teaches: There was a case with רבי נהוראי, who went with the witness to vouch for him on שבת in אושא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the conclusion that two are needed. It brings a story where רבי נהוראי seems to have vouched by himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only רבי נהוראי is mentioned in the story, which suggests a single voucher was accepted. That would contradict רב פפא's 'another pair'.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא, a sage of the משנה period
אושא, the city where the סנהדרין sat at that time

phrases.notes: The reverse of the question in step 1.

phrases.english: But it was taught: An incident with Rabbi Nehorai
who went along with the witness

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that two people are needed to vouch for a witness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נהוראי apparently vouched alone, so one should be enough.

steps.title: Another witness was with him but went unnamed out of respect
steps.stepSummary: The Sages answer that a second witness accompanied רבי נהוראי. He was not mentioned out of honor for רבי נהוראי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: רבי נהוראי had another witness with him. The reason he was not counted in the story is out of respect for רבי נהוראי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: there really were two vouchers, but the story only names רבי נהוראי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of two stays in place. The ברייתא left out the second witness so it would not seem to put him on the same level as the great רבי נהוראי.

phrases.english: and the fact that it did not count him —
is because of the honor of Rabbi Nehorai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי סָהֲדָא אַחֲרִינָא הֲוָה בַּהֲדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the facts of the story (an unmentioned second witness)
steps.terutzMaskana: A second witness traveled with him but was left out of the story out of respect.

steps.title: רב אשי: the second witness was already in אושא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers differently: the second witness was already in אושא, and רבי נהוראי traveled there to join him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The other witness was in אושא, and רבי נהוראי went there to join with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second answer to the same challenge. No second voucher traveled with רבי נהוראי. A partner voucher was already waiting in אושא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer also keeps the rule of two. The story only describes רבי נהוראי traveling because the other voucher was already at the court. רבי נהוראי's testimony joined his to make a full pair.

keyTerms.meaning: to join together, to combine (as a pair of witnesses)

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers agree that vouching needs two people. They only differ on where the second witness was in the רבי נהוראי story.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי סָהֲדָא אַחֲרִינָא הֲוָה בְּאוּשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי נהוראי was the only voucher.
steps.terutzMaskana: A second witness was already in אושא, and רבי נהוראי joined him to form a pair.

steps.title: What does the story teach if the second witness was already there?
steps.stepSummary: On רב אשי's answer, the גמרא asks what new lesson the story of רבי נהוראי teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of telling us this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב אשי's answer from Step 8. If the second witness was already waiting in אושא, the story of רבי נהוראי seems to teach nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that two witnesses may break שבת to testify about the new moon. If רבי נהוראי simply joined a witness who was already there, the case looks ordinary. So why would the ברייתא bother to record it?

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your explanation is correct)
What is the point of saying this? (it seems obvious)

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of saying it?
phrases.notes: Refers back to רב אשי's explanation that the second witness was already in אושא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what is gained from the ברייתא if רב אשי's reading is correct.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new חידוש the story of רבי נהוראי teaches, if it is just two witnesses meeting to testify.

steps.title: שבת may be broken even when it is uncertain the trip is needed
steps.stepSummary: The story teaches that you may break שבת for עדות החודש even when you are not sure the trip will be useful.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that we do not break שבת in a case of doubt. So it teaches us that we do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 9. The story teaches that one may break שבת to testify even when it is not certain the testimony will be needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נהוראי could not be sure the other witness would still be in אושא, or would actually testify. He traveled anyway, so the trip might have turned out to be useless. The lesson is that for the new moon, even a doubtful need is enough to permit breaking שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a wrong assumption)

steps.whatToRemember: For עדות החודש, שבת may be broken even when it is uncertain that the testimony will be needed.

phrases.english: in a case of doubt we do not break Shabbat,
phrases.notes: The doubt is whether the other witness would still be there and would testify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא teaches that one may break Shabbat for the new moon even in a case of doubt.

steps.title: עולא reports that the month was declared in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: עולא comes to בבל and reports by himself that the month was declared in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When עולא came, he said: They declared the new month in the West (ארץ ישראל).
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. עולא, alone, brings news that בית דין in ארץ ישראל declared the new month, and this sets up רב כהנא's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we needed two witnesses to testify that they saw the moon. Here it is different: one person reports that בית דין already declared the month. The question is whether one person is enough for that.

keyTerms.meaning: When (he) came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: They sanctified the month in the West.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: reporting that the month was already declared, as opposed to testifying about seeing the moon.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולא's single report that the month was declared in ארץ ישראל was accepted.

steps.title: Any single person is believed about the declared month
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says that even an ordinary person is believed alone, because people do not lie about things that will come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: Of course עולא is believed, since he is a great man. But even an ordinary person is believed. Why? Because people do not lie about something that is going to be revealed anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא explains why עולא was believed alone. It was not because he was a great scholar. Anyone would be believed, and he gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think עולא was believed only because of his greatness. רב כהנא widens the rule to every person. Whether the month was declared is something everyone will soon find out, so a lie would be quickly exposed, and people do not lie in such cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter that is going to be revealed

steps.confusionAlert: This is not testimony about seeing the moon, which needs two witnesses because it is called משפט. This is only reporting a public fact that בית דין already declared, so one person is enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of מילתא דעבידא לאגלויי, that people do not lie about things that will be found out, is a general rule of believability used in many places in ש״ס.

phrases.english: it is not necessary to say about Ulla,
who is a great man, that he is believed.
Any matter that is going to be revealed,
people do not lie about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and widens the acceptance of עולא's report in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any single person is believed to report that the month was declared, because people do not lie about something that will be revealed.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that one person who comes from far away and reports the month was declared is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: If one person comes from the end of the world and says that בית דין declared the month, he is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב כהנא said. This backs up his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'one person' and gives no requirement that he be a great man. That matches רב כהנא's point that even an ordinary single person is believed about the declaration of the month.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports this)
The end of the world, meaning a far-off place

steps.whatToRemember: One person is believed to report that בית דין declared the month (רב כהנא, supported by a ברייתא).

phrases.english: if one person came from the end of the world

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר קִדְּשׁוּ בֵּית דִּין אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ —
phrases.english: and said: the court sanctified the month,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב כהנא's rule from Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רב כהנא's rule that one ordinary person is believed about the declared month.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: one person who comes from far away and reports the declaration is believed.

steps.title: The גמרא returns to the משנה about accepting any witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that at first, testimony about the month was accepted from anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, they would accept testimony about the new month from any person, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes a new line of the משנה so it can explain it. This sets up the ברייתא about the בייתוסין that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says testimony was once accepted from anyone, until the בייתוסין caused trouble, and then only from known people. The גמרא is about to explain what trouble they caused.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony about seeing the new moon
Etc. (the quote continues in the משנה)

phrases.english: testimony of the month from any person, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מְקַבְּלִין עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ מִכׇּל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next topic in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally, testimony about the new moon was accepted from anyone, until the בייתוסין corrupted the process.

steps.title: The בייתוסין hire two false witnesses
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the בייתוסין paid two men 400 זוז to testify falsely about the new moon.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: What was the damage the בייתוסין did? Once they tried to trick the חכמים. They hired two people for 400 זוז, one of our people and one of theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that tells the story behind the משנה. The בייתוסין bribed two people to give false testimony about the new moon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בייתוסין wanted the month fixed on a wrong day, to suit their own views about the calendar and the festivals. They hired one man from their own group and one from the faithful Jews, so that the testimony would look trustworthy.

keyTerms.meaning: The בייתוסין, a sect that rejected the חכמים' tradition

phrases.english: What corruption did the Boethusians cause?
one of ours and one of theirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מָה קִלְקוּל קִלְקְלוּ הַבַּיְיתּוֹסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the corruption mentioned in the משנה of Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בייתוסין bribed two witnesses to give false testimony about the new moon.

steps.title: Our witness gives a deliberately absurd description
steps.stepSummary: Their witness testifies and leaves. Our witness, when questioned, describes the 'moon' as if it were an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their witness gave his testimony and left. They asked ours: Tell us how you saw the moon. He said: I was going up at מעלה אדומים and saw it crouching between two rocks. Its head was like a calf, its ears like a young goat, its horns like a deer, and its tail was lying between its thighs. I looked at it, got scared, and fell backward.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The faithful witness, when questioned in the usual way, gives a silly description of an animal instead of the moon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית דין always questioned witnesses about how they saw the moon. Our witness made the description absurd on purpose, describing a strange animal. This signaled to the חכמים that his testimony was not real.

keyTerms.meaning: מעלה אדומים, an ascent near ירושלים

phrases.english: Theirs gave his testimony and left.
Say how you saw the moon!
I was going up at Ma'ale Adumim,

phrases.aramaic: וּרְאִיתִיו שֶׁהוּא רָבוּץ בֵּין שְׁנֵי סְלָעִים,
phrases.english: and I saw it crouching between two rocks,
its ears like a kid goat,
and its tail resting between its thighs,
and I peeked at it and was startled

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the two hired witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The faithful witness undermined the plot by giving an obviously absurd description.

steps.title: Our witness reveals the bribe
steps.stepSummary: The faithful witness shows the 200 זוז he was paid, exposing the plot.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you do not believe me, here are 200 זוז tied up in my cloak.
steps.whatsHappening: The witness ends by revealing the money he was paid, proving the whole testimony was a bribery plot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each witness received half of the 400 זוז, which is 200. By showing his share, the faithful witness proved to the חכמים that the בייתוסין had bribed false witnesses. This explains why the משנה says they stopped accepting testimony from just anyone.
steps.whatToRemember: Because the בייתוסין bribed false witnesses, בית דין stopped accepting testimony about the new moon from unknown people.

phrases.english: And if you do not believe me,
wrapped up for me in my cloak.
phrases.notes: His half of the 400 זוז bribe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the witness's statement and exposes the plot.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bribe was exposed, which shows why the משנה restricted who may testify.

steps.title: The Sages ask the honest witness why he got involved
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask the faithful witness what pushed him to take part, and he explains he joined the plot only to expose it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'Who made you do this?' He said to them: 'I heard that the בייתוסין wanted to trick the חכמים. I said to myself: I will go and let them know, so that unworthy people do not come and trick the חכמים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask the honest witness why he took the bribe, and he answers that he did it to warn them. He was never really on the side of the בייתוסין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He took the money on purpose so he could get inside the plot. His fear was that other, dishonest witnesses would come and fool the court. This explains why he should not be treated as a guilty party.

keyTerms.meaning: made you do it / pushed you into this
the בייתוסים, a group that rejected the חכמים' tradition

phrases.english: They said to him: Who pushed you into this?
He said to them: I heard
that the Boethusians wanted to mislead the Sages,
I said: I will go and let them know,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא יָבוֹאוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁאֵינָם מְהוּגָּנִין

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after the witness showed the 200 זוז.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the honest witness took part in the false testimony plot.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He joined only to find out the plot and warn the חכמים, so they would not be fooled.

steps.title: The reward, the punishment, and the new rule about witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The witness keeps the 200 זוז as a gift. The hirer is to be lashed. From then on, only known witnesses are accepted for the new moon.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'The 200 זוז are given to you as a gift, and the one who hired you will be stretched on the post for lashes.' At that time they made a rule to accept testimony only from people they knew.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a verdict and a new rule. Because of the plot, the בית דין now accepts new-moon testimony only from witnesses it knows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the source of the change mentioned in the משנה from step 14. Earlier, testimony was accepted from anyone. Now there is a תקנה limiting it to known people. The story shows exactly why the old open policy had to end.

keyTerms.meaning: will be stretched on the post (for lashes)
people who are known (to the court)

steps.whatToRemember: The בייתוסין plot is the reason for the תקנה to accept new-moon witnesses only from people the בית דין knows.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains the 'בראשונה' (at first) wording in the משנה: an open policy was later narrowed because of a real attempt to trick the court.

phrases.english: They said to him: The two hundred zuz —
are given to you as a gift,
and the one who hired you shall be stretched on the post.
except from those who were known.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the verdict after the witness explains himself, and closes the story with a תקנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: New-moon testimony is accepted only from witnesses known to the בית דין, because of the בייתוסין plot.

steps.title: New משנה: torches were replaced by messengers
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that at first they lit signal torches to announce the new month. After the כותים ruined this, messengers were sent instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: At first they used to light signal torches. Once the כותים ruined this, they made a rule that messengers should go out.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about how news of the new month reached far-away places. It describes another change: torches first, then messengers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the last section: an old system was changed because people abused it. The כותים lit fake torches to confuse the Jews, so the חכמים switched to sending people.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה (a new משנה starts here)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the troublemakers are the כותים, not the בייתוסין from the story before. These are two different groups and two different problems: false witnesses and false torches.

phrases.english: At first they would light signal torches.
they instituted that messengers should go out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. Like the earlier story, it tells of a system changed because of abuse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First torches announced the new month. After the כותים corrupted this, messengers were sent instead.

steps.title: How the signal torches were made and used
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains how the torch was built and waved on a mountaintop until the next mountain answered, passing the message along.
steps.simpleTranslation: How would they light the torches? They brought long cedar poles, reeds, pinewood, and beaten flax, and tied them with a string. Someone climbed to the top of the mountain, lit them, and waved the fire back and forth and up and down, until he saw his friend doing the same on the second mountain, and the same on the third mountain.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks 'how did they do it?' and answers right away with the details. It describes building the torch and waving it from mountain to mountain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The materials are things that burn brightly. The waving makes the signal clear and separate from an ordinary fire. Each person waits until the next mountain answers, so a chain of fires carries the news far away.

phrases.english: How would they light the torches?
They bring long poles of cedar,
And he ties them with a string
and goes up to the top of the mountain
And he waves it back and forth and up and down,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה כֵּן בְּרֹאשׁ הָהָר הַשֵּׁנִי,
phrases.english: doing the same on the top of the second mountain,
and likewise on the top of the third mountain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the torch system from step 20 actually worked.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical method for lighting and passing on the משואות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bright-burning materials tied together, lit on a mountaintop, and waved until the next mountain answered, forming a chain.

steps.title: The mountain-to-mountain route of the torches
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the chain of mountains that passed the torch signal: from הר המשחה to סרטבא, then גרופינא, then חוורן, then בית בלתין.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where did they light the torches? From הר המשחה to סרטבא, from סרטבא to גרופינא, from גרופינא to חוורן, and from חוורן to בית בלתין.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its description of the torch system. It names the exact mountains that relayed the signal, one after another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 explained how one torch was waved until the next mountain answered. Here the משנה gives the actual route. The signal left ירושלים from הר המשחה and passed through four more mountaintops, each one picking up the message from the one before it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Mount of Olives, beside ירושלים, where the relay started
בית בלתין, the last fixed station on the route

phrases.english: And from where would they light the torches?
From the Mount of Olives to Sartava,
and from Chavran to Beit Baltin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of the torch system by giving the route.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The signal traveled along a fixed chain: הר המשחה, סרטבא, גרופינא, חוורן, בית בלתין.

steps.title: From the last mountain, the whole Diaspora lights up
steps.stepSummary: At בית בלתין the fixed route ends. The signaler waves his torch in every direction until he sees the entire גולה lit up like one big bonfire.
steps.simpleTranslation: From בית בלתין they did not move on to another fixed spot. Instead, the man waved the torch back and forth and up and down, until he saw the whole גולה in front of him glowing like one bonfire.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes describing the relay. After the last fixed mountain, the message spreads outward to all the Jewish communities of the גולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to בית בלתין, the signal went in a single line. From there it fanned out: the signaler waved in all directions, many places lit their own fires in reply, and together they looked like one huge fire.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not move from there to another fixed station
Waving back and forth and up and down

steps.whatToRemember: The torch relay went in one fixed line of mountains up to בית בלתין. From there the signal spread out until the whole גולה was lit like one big fire.

phrases.english: And from Beit Baltin they did not move from there,
rather, he would wave it back and forth and up and down

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁהָיָה רוֹאֶה כׇּל הַגּוֹלָה לְפָנָיו
phrases.english: until he would see the entire Diaspora before him

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the route by explaining what happened at the final station.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From בית בלתין, the signal spread in all directions until the whole גולה received it.

steps.title: How do we know 'משיאין' means lighting a fire?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for a source showing that the משנה's word משיאין means 'to set alight.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we see that the word 'משיאין' means burning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה with a word question. It wants proof that משיאין means lighting a fire, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The root נשא usually means 'to lift' or 'to carry,' so it is not obvious that it means 'to kindle.' The גמרא wants a source for this meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
An expression, a type of wording

phrases.english: that 'masi'in' is an expression of burning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא, starting with the meaning of the משנה's key word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source proving that משיאין means kindling.

steps.title: Proof from the verse about דוד and its Aramaic translation
steps.stepSummary: The verse says וישאם דוד, and the תרגום translates it as ואוקדינון, 'and he burned them.' So the root נשא can mean burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And דוד and his men וישאם [took them away],' and we translate it in Aramaic: 'And דוד burned them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. It brings a פסוק whose standard Aramaic translation shows that the same root means 'burned.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמואל ב, דוד takes the idols left behind by the פלשתים. The תרגום reads וישאם as 'he burned them.' Since that verse uses the same root, משיאין in the משנה can mean lighting fires.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'and he carried them,' here understood as 'and he burned them'
We translate, referring to the standard Aramaic תרגום

steps.confusionAlert: Don't be thrown by the plain meaning of the verse, 'carried them off.' The proof comes from the Aramaic תרגום, which reads the same word as 'burned.'

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And David and his men vayisa'em,'
and we translate: 'And David burned them.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the word question from step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תרגום of וישאם as ואוקדינון shows the root means burning.

steps.title: Torches only for a month declared on time
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that torches were lit only when the new month was sanctified on time, on the 30th day. They were lit on the night after that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Torches were lit only for a month whose new moon was seen at its proper time, to sanctify it. And when were they lit? On the night after it, at the start of what would have been the extra day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that limits the torch system. Torches were used only in one specific situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Seen at its proper time' means the new moon was seen on the 30th day. That day became ראש חודש, which left the previous month short (חסר, 29 days). The torches were lit the following night, the night after ראש חודש.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this introduces a ברייתא
At its proper time, on the 30th day
To sanctify it as ראש חודש
On the night of its 'extra' day, the night after ראש חודש

phrases.english: except for a month whose moon was seen at its proper time
And when do they light them?
On the night of its additional day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: when the torches were actually used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torches were lit only when ראש חודש fell on the 30th day (after a חסר month), on the night after it.

steps.title: Why no torches for a full month?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the conclusion that torches were lit after a short month but not after a full one, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: This means that for a short month we do the lighting, but for a full month we do not. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what the ברייתא implies and asks why the rule works that way. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both kinds of month need to be announced to the people far away, so leaving out the full month seems odd. The גמרא asks what lies behind this one-sided rule.

phrases.english: Is this to say that for a deficient month we perform it,
but for a full month we do not perform it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the ברייתא and asks for its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why torches were lit only after a חסר month and never after a מלא month.

steps.title: רבי זירא: a safeguard because of ראש חודש on ערב שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that this is a גזירה. If ראש חודש after a short month falls on Friday, the torches can only be lit on מוצאי שבת. Lighting torches for full months too would lead people to a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: It is a decree because of a ראש חודש after a short month that falls on Friday. When would they light then? On Saturday night. Because if you say we also light for a full month, people would come...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא begins answering why there are no torches for a full month. The sentence is cut off at the end of the amud, and the rest of his reasoning continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the torches go up on the night right after ראש חודש. If ראש חודש is on Friday, that night is שבת, when lighting a fire is forbidden, so the lighting is pushed to Saturday night. רבי זירא is starting to show that if full months also got torches, Saturday-night torches could be misread, and people would come to a wrong conclusion about the date.

keyTerms.meaning: They will come to (make a mistake)

steps.confusionAlert: The step ends in the middle of a sentence ('people would come...'). The rest of רבי זירא's reasoning appears on the next amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the חכמים designing a public signal system so that it could never send a mixed message about the date of ראש חודש.

phrases.english: It is a decree because of a New Moon after a deficient month
When do they perform it? At the conclusion of Shabbat.
For if you say we should perform it for a full month as well,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה tied to ראש חודש on ערב שבת, whose torches are delayed to מוצאי שבת; lighting for full months too would cause confusion (completed on the next amud).
